reason: Jamku charges only ₹6,500 a year, so ₹12,990 is double the price for my 2-person practice when I have avoided third-party cloud tools for years out of fear of data leaks. While keeping files in our own Google Drive sounds promising, I will only test the free 2-seat pilot first to verify data security before paying twice what established alternatives charge.
objection: Jamku charges only ₹6,500 a year—why is Docketra more expensive, and can I truly trust that connecting Google Drive won't compromise confidential client ITR and ROC files?
would_change_my_mind: Pricing closer to Jamku around ₹7,000 to ₹8,000 a year, combined with undeniable proof during the free pilot that our confidential client files remain strictly isolated and leakproof in our own Google Drive.
